headline: A preprint reports distributed agents scaling interpretation of a whole-brain perturbation atlas
summary: A bioRxiv preprint and Oct 21 OpenAI research report describe distributed biological reasoning: thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents separately analyzed perturbations in an existing whole-brain Perturb-seq atlas and combined results into a reasoning atlas. The authors report a 32-minute analysis; R&D World reports 1,946 agents and 7,586 cited references versus about 11 in a same-model, same-tools single-agent comparison at the largest workload. It reports that 30 doctoral-level biologists preferred distributed reports in 45 of 60 head-to-head judgments and that agents matched or refined 48 of 55 atlas findings recoverable from their inputs. These remain author-reported results from one dataset, not independent reproduction. The DCTN1/cholesterol lead's origin is disputed across the OpenAI article and R&D World account; it remains a hypothesis, not an established biological mechanism.
